title: Annotatio II §.VI: Hard to state without Pelagian tinge — Tossanus and Tanner accuse Hunnius; Calixtus Thorun/Gratia refs
pass_a_gloss: But it is difficult to propose this Sentence thus, so that it may not seem to have something akin to Pelagianism — just as indeed both Daniel Tossanus the Calvinist and Adam Tanner the Jesuit accuse Hunnius of Pelagianism. In the place cited, number 22. Compare the same Calixtus's Consideration of Reformed Doctrine according to the Thorun Confession, on Grace, p. 62.
pass_b_english: Still, it is hard to set out that teaching without seeming to shade toward Pelagianism — and Daniel Tossanus the Calvinist and Adam Tanner the Jesuit both charge Hunnius with Pelagianism (cited place, no. 22).
See also the same Calixtus, Consideration of Reformed Doctrine according to the Thorun Confession, on Grace, p. 62.
source_text: Difficile autem est, Sententiam hanc ita proponere, ne quid Pelagianismo affine habere videatur, quemadmodum sanè Pelagianismi Hunnium accusant, tum Daniel Tossanus Calvinista, tùm Adamus Tannerus Jesuita. cit. loc, num. 22. Confer ejusdem Calixti Considerat. Doct. Reform, juxta Confess. Thoruniens. de Gratia p. 62.
